correctness.rationale: For each nonempty base face sigma, set u_sigma=[a,sigma] and z_sigma=partial u_sigma. The basis (apex,z_sigma,u_sigma) is unimodular because z_sigma has leading coefficient +1 on the corresponding non-apex face. Global minimality of the apex makes both this basis change and its inverse filtration-preserving even with tied weights. Each differential is exactly u_sigma -> z_sigma with coefficient one, so the integral persistent chain complex splits into primitive two-term summands with entrance grades b_sigma=max_w(sigma)+h(dim sigma) and d_sigma=max_w(sigma)+h(dim sigma+1), plus an essential apex. Finite-field verifier independently compared 945 complete barcodes in primes 2, 3, 5; these tests are not substituted for the integral proof. A one-edge nonminimum-apex example shows why that hypothesis is essential.

value.rationale: ELSF was introduced to reveal topological features suppressed by simultaneous entrance, so cones over arbitrary bases with a globally minimal dominating vertex are a mathematically natural negative control. The theorem gives all weights, dimensions, exact integral inclusion maps and fixed finite bar length epsilon. On a full m-simplex base it creates 2^m-1 finite bars despite contractibility. Two flag bases with equal face counts but distinct H1 have identical all-zero-weight cone barcodes, exposing a meaningful interpretive limitation of this recently proposed filter. This is a structural boundary, not merely code-generated examples or a renaming of a textbook result.
